               A001333   Pell-Lucas numbers: numerators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(2).
(Formerly M2665 N1064)    367     1, 1, 3, 7, 17, 41, 99, 239, 577, 1393, 3363, 8119, 19601, 47321, 114243, 275807, 665857, 1607521, 3880899, 9369319, 22619537, 54608393, 131836323, 318281039, 768398401, 1855077841, 4478554083, 10812186007, 26102926097, 63018038201, 152139002499, 367296043199  ([list](https://oeis.org/A001333/list); [graph](https://oeis.org/A001333/graph); [refs](https://oeis.org/search?q=A001333+-id:A001333); [listen](https://oeis.org/A001333/listen); [history](https://oeis.org/history?seq=A001333); [text](https://oeis.org/search?q=id:A001333&fmt=text); [internal format](https://oeis.org/A001333/internal))      OFFSET  0,3    COMMENTS  Number of n-step non-selfintersecting paths starting at (0,0) with steps of types (1,0), (-1,0) or (0,1) [Stanley]. Number of n steps one-sided prudent walks with east, west and north steps. - [Shanzhen Gao](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Shanzhen_Gao), Apr 26 2011 Number of ternary strings of length n-1 with subwords (0,2) and (2,0) not allowed. - [Olivier Gérard](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Olivier_G%C3%A9rard), Aug 28 2012 Number of symmetric 2n X 2 or (2n-1) X 2 crossword puzzle grids: all white squares are edge connected; at least 1 white square on every edge of grid; 180-degree rotational symmetry. - [Erich Friedman](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Erich_Friedman) a(n+1) is the number of ways to put molecules on a 2 X n ladder lattice so that the molecules do not touch each other. In other words, a(n+1) is the number of independent vertex sets and vertex covers in the n-ladder graph P_2 X P_n. - [Eric W. Weisstein](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Eric_W._Weisstein), Apr 04 2017 Number of (n-1) X 2 binary arrays with a path of adjacent 1's from top row to bottom row, see [A359576](https://oeis.org/A359576). - [R. H. Hardin](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:R._H._Hardin), Mar 16 2002 a(2*n+1) with b(2*n+1) := [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(2*n+1), n >= 0, give all (positive integer) solutions to Pell equation a^2 - 2*b^2 = -1. a(2*n) with b(2*n) := [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(2*n), n >= 1, give all (positive integer) solutions to Pell equation a^2 - 2*b^2 = +1 (see Emerson reference). Bisection: a(2*n) = T(n,3) = [A001541](https://oeis.org/A001541)(n), n >= 0 and a(2*n+1) = S(2*n,2*sqrt(2)) = [A002315](https://oeis.org/A002315)(n), n >= 0, with T(n,x), resp. S(n,x), Chebyshev's polynomials of the first, resp. second kind. See [A053120](https://oeis.org/A053120), resp. [A049310](https://oeis.org/A049310). Binomial transform of [A077957](https://oeis.org/A077957). - [Paul Barry](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Paul_Barry), Feb 25 2003 For n > 0, the number of (s(0), s(1), ..., s(n)) such that 0 < s(i) < 4 and |s(i) - s(i-1)| <= 1 for i = 1,2,...,n, s(0) = 2, s(n) = 2. - [Herbert Kociemba](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Herbert_Kociemba), Jun 02 2004 For n > 1, a(n) corresponds to the longer side of a near right-angled isosceles triangle, one of the equal sides being [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n). - [Lekraj Beedassy](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Lekraj_Beedassy), Aug 06 2004 Exponents of terms in the series F(x,1), where F is determined by the equation F(x,y) = xy + F(x^2*y,x). - [Jonathan Sondow](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Jonathan_Sondow), Dec 18 2004 Number of n-words from the alphabet A={0,1,2} which two neighbors differ by at most 1. - Fung Cheok Yin (cheokyin_restart(AT)yahoo.com.hk), Aug 30 2006 Consider the mapping f(a/b) = (a + 2b)/(a + b). Taking a = b = 1 to start with and carrying out this mapping repeatedly on each new (reduced) rational number gives the following sequence 1/1, 3/2, 7/5, 17/12, 41/29, ... converging to 2^(1/2). Sequence contains the numerators. - [Amarnath Murthy](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Amarnath_Murthy), Mar 22 2003 [Amended by Paul E. Black (paul.black(AT)nist.gov), Dec 18 2006] Odd-indexed prime numerators are prime RMS numbers ([A140480](https://oeis.org/A140480)) and also NSW primes ([A088165](https://oeis.org/A088165)). - [Ctibor O. Zizka](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Ctibor_O._Zizka), Aug 13 2008 The intermediate convergents to 2^(1/2) begin with 4/3, 10/7, 24/17, 58/41; essentially, numerators=[A052542](https://oeis.org/A052542) and denominators here. - [Clark Kimberling](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Clark_Kimberling), Aug 26 2008 Equals right border of triangle [A143966](https://oeis.org/A143966). Starting (1, 3, 7, ...) equals INVERT transform of (1, 2, 2, 2, ...) and row sums of triangle [A143966](https://oeis.org/A143966). - [Gary W. Adamson](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Gary_W._Adamson), Sep 06 2008 Inverse binomial transform of [A006012](https://oeis.org/A006012); Hankel transform is := [1, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, ...]. - [Philippe Deléham](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Philippe_Del%C3%A9ham), Dec 04 2008 From [Charlie Marion](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Charlie_Marion), Jan 07 2009: (Start) In general, denominators, a(k,n) and numerators, b(k,n), of continued fraction convergents to sqrt((k+1)/k) may be found as follows: let a(k,0) = 1, a(k,1) = 2k; for n>0, a(k,2n) = 2*a(k,2n-1) + a(k,2n-2) and a(k,2n+1) = (2k)*a(k,2n) + a(k,2n-1); let b(k,0) = 1, b(k,1) = 2k+1; for n>0, b(k,2n) = 2*b(k,2n-1) + b(k,2n-2) and b(k,2n+1) = (2k)*b(k,2n) + b(k,2n-1). For example, the convergents to sqrt(2/1) start 1/1, 3/2, 7/5, 17/12, 41/29. In general, if a(k,n) and b(k,n) are the denominators and numerators, respectively, of continued fraction convergents to sqrt((k+1)/k) as defined above, then k*a(k,2n)^2 - a(k,2n-1)*a(k,2n+1) = k = k*a(k,2n-2)*a(k,2n) - a(k,2n-1)^2 and b(k,2n-1)*b(k,2n+1) - k*b(k,2n)^2 = k+1 = b(k,2n-1)^2 - k*b(k,2n-2)*b(k,2n); for example, if k=1 and n=3, then b(1,n)=a(n+1) and 1*a(1,6)^2 - a(1,5)*a(1,7) = 1*169^2 - 70*408 = 1; 1*a(1,4)*a(1,6) - a(1,5)^2 = 1*29*169 - 70^2 = 1; b(1,5)*b(1,7) - 1*b(1,6)^2 = 99*577 - 1*239^2 = 2; b(1,5)^2 - 1*b(1,4)*b(1,6) = 99^2 - 1*41*239 = 2. Cf. [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129), [A142238](https://oeis.org/A142238)-[A142239](https://oeis.org/A142239), [A153313](https://oeis.org/A153313)-[A153318](https://oeis.org/A153318). (End) This sequence occurs in the lower bound of the order of the set of equivalent resistances of n equal resistors combined in series and in parallel ([A048211](https://oeis.org/A048211)). - [Sameen Ahmed Khan](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Sameen_Ahmed_Khan), Jun 28 2010 Let M = a triangle with the Fibonacci series in each column, but the leftmost column is shifted upwards one row. [A001333](https://oeis.org/A001333) = lim_{n->infinity} M^n, the left-shifted vector considered as a sequence. - [Gary W. Adamson](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Gary_W._Adamson), Jul 27 2010 a(n) is the number of compositions of n when there are 1 type of 1 and 2 types of other natural numbers. - [Milan Janjic](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Milan_Janjic), Aug 13 2010 Equals the INVERTi transform of [A055099](https://oeis.org/A055099). - [Gary W. Adamson](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Gary_W._Adamson), Aug 14 2010 From [L. Edson Jeffery](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:L._Edson_Jeffery), Apr 04 2011: (Start) Let U be the unit-primitive matrix (see [Jeffery]) U = U_(8,2) = (0 0 1 0)  (0 1 0 1)  (1 0 2 0)  (0 2 0 1). Then a(n) = (1/4)*Trace(U^n). (See also [A084130](https://oeis.org/A084130), [A006012](https://oeis.org/A006012).) (End) For n >= 1, row sums of triangle  m/k.|..0.....1.....2.....3.....4.....5.....6.....7  ==================================================  .0..|..1  .1..|..1.....2  .2..|..1.....2.....4  .3..|..1.....4.....4.....8  .4..|..1.....4....12.....8....16  .5..|..1.....6....12....32....16....32  .6..|..1.....6....24....32....80....32....64  .7..|..1.....8....24....80....80...192....64...128 which is the triangle for numbers 2^k*C(m,k) with duplicated diagonals. - [Vladimir Shevelev](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Vladimir_Shevelev), Apr 12 2012 a(n) is also the number of ways to place k non-attacking wazirs on a 2 X n board, summed over all k >= 0 (a wazir is a leaper [0,1]). - [Vaclav Kotesovec](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Vaclav_Kotesovec), May 08 2012 The sequences a(n) and b(n) := [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n) are entries of powers of the special case of the Brahmagupta Matrix - for details see Suryanarayan's paper. Further, as Suryanarayan remark, if we set A = 2*(a(n) + b(n))*b(n), B = a(n)*(a(n) + 2*b(n)), C = a(n)^2 + 2*a(n)*b(n) + 2*b(n)^2 we obtain integral solutions of the Pythagorean relation A^2 + B^2 = C^2, where A and B are consecutive integers. - [Roman Witula](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Roman_Witula), Jul 28 2012 Pisano period lengths: 1, 1, 8, 4, 12, 8, 6, 4, 24, 12, 24, 8, 28, 6, 24, 8, 16, 24, 40, 12, .... - [R. Mathar](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:R._J._Mathar), Feb 03 2014 If p is prime, a(p) == 1 (mod p) (compare with similar comment for [A000032](https://oeis.org/A000032)). - [Creighton Dement](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Creighton_Dement), Oct 11 2005, modified by [Davide Colazingari](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Davide_Colazingari), Jun 26 2016 a(n) = [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n) + [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n-1), where [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n) is the n-th Pell Number; e.g., a(6) = 99 = [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(6) + [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(5) = 70 + 29. Hence the sequence of fractions has the form 1 + [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n-1)/[A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n), and the ratio [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n-1)/[A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n)converges to sqrt(2) - 1. - [Gregory L. Simay](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Gregory_L._Simay), Nov 30 2018 For n > 0, a(n+1) is the length of tau^n(1) where tau is the morphism: 1 -> 101, 0 -> 1. G.f.: (1 - x) / (1 - 2*x - x^2) = 1 / (1 - x / (1 - 2*x / (1 + x))). - [Simon Plouffe](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Simon_Plouffe) in his 1992 dissertation. [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(2n) = 2*[A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n)*a(n). - [John McNamara](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:John_McNamara), Oct 30 2002 a(n) = (-i)^n * T(n, i), with T(n, x) Chebyshev's polynomials of the first kind [A053120](https://oeis.org/A053120) and i^2 = -1. a(n) = a(n-1) + [A052542](https://oeis.org/A052542)(n-1), n>1. a(n)/[A052542](https://oeis.org/A052542)(n) converges to sqrt(1/2). - Mario Catalani (mario.catalani(AT)unito.it), Apr 29 2003 E.g.f.: exp(x)cosh(x*sqrt(2)). - [Paul Barry](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Paul_Barry), May 08 2003 a(n) = Sum_{k=0..floor(n/2)} binomial(n, 2k)2^k. - [Paul Barry](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Paul_Barry), May 13 2003 For n > 0, a(n)^2 - (1 + (-1)^(n))/2 = Sum_{k=0..n-1} ((2k+1)*[A001653](https://oeis.org/A001653)(n-1-k));                A001333   Pell-Lucas numbers: numerators of continued fraction convergents to sqrt(2).
(Formerly M2665 N1064)    367     1, 1, 3, 7, 17, 41, 99, 239, 577, 1393, 3363, 8119, 19601, 47321, 114243, 275807, 665857, 1607521, 3880899, 9369319, 22619537, 54608393, 131836323, 318281039, 768398401, 1855077841, 4478554083, 10812186007, 26102926097, 63018038201, 152139002499, 367296043199  ([list](https://oeis.org/A001333/list); [graph](https://oeis.org/A001333/graph); [refs](https://oeis.org/search?q=A001333+-id:A001333); [listen](https://oeis.org/A001333/listen); [history](https://oeis.org/history?seq=A001333); [text](https://oeis.org/search?q=id:A001333&fmt=text); [internal format](https://oeis.org/A001333/internal))      OFFSET  0,3    COMMENTS  Number of n-step non-selfintersecting paths starting at (0,0) with steps of types (1,0), (-1,0) or (0,1) [Stanley]. Number of n steps one-sided prudent walks with east, west and north steps. - [Shanzhen Gao](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Shanzhen_Gao), Apr 26 2011 Number of ternary strings of length n-1 with subwords (0,2) and (2,0) not allowed. - [Olivier Gérard](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Olivier_G%C3%A9rard), Aug 28 2012 Number of symmetric 2n X 2 or (2n-1) X 2 crossword puzzle grids: all white squares are edge connected; at least 1 white square on every edge of grid; 180-degree rotational symmetry. - [Erich Friedman](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Erich_Friedman) a(n+1) is the number of ways to put molecules on a 2 X n ladder lattice so that the molecules do not touch each other. In other words, a(n+1) is the number of independent vertex sets and vertex covers in the n-ladder graph P_2 X P_n. - [Eric W. Weisstein](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Eric_W._Weisstein), Apr 04 2017 Number of (n-1) X 2 binary arrays with a path of adjacent 1's from top row to bottom row, see [A359576](https://oeis.org/A359576). - [R. H. Hardin](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:R._H._Hardin), Mar 16 2002 a(2*n+1) with b(2*n+1) := [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(2*n+1), n >= 0, give all (positive integer) solutions to Pell equation a^2 - 2*b^2 = -1. a(2*n) with b(2*n) := [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(2*n), n >= 1, give all (positive integer) solutions to Pell equation a^2 - 2*b^2 = +1 (see Emerson reference). Bisection: a(2*n) = T(n,3) = [A001541](https://oeis.org/A001541)(n), n >= 0 and a(2*n+1) = S(2*n,2*sqrt(2)) = [A002315](https://oeis.org/A002315)(n), n >= 0, with T(n,x), resp. S(n,x), Chebyshev's polynomials of the first, resp. second kind. See [A053120](https://oeis.org/A053120), resp. [A049310](https://oeis.org/A049310). Binomial transform of [A077957](https://oeis.org/A077957). - [Paul Barry](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Paul_Barry), Feb 25 2003 For n > 0, the number of (s(0), s(1), ..., s(n)) such that 0 < s(i) < 4 and |s(i) - s(i-1)| <= 1 for i = 1,2,...,n, s(0) = 2, s(n) = 2. - [Herbert Kociemba](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Herbert_Kociemba), Jun 02 2004 For n > 1, a(n) corresponds to the longer side of a near right-angled isosceles triangle, one of the equal sides being [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n). - [Lekraj Beedassy](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Lekraj_Beedassy), Aug 06 2004 Exponents of terms in the series F(x,1), where F is determined by the equation F(x,y) = xy + F(x^2*y,x). - [Jonathan Sondow](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Jonathan_Sondow), Dec 18 2004 Number of n-words from the alphabet A={0,1,2} which two neighbors differ by at most 1. - Fung Cheok Yin (cheokyin_restart(AT)yahoo.com.hk), Aug 30 2006 Consider the mapping f(a/b) = (a + 2b)/(a + b). Taking a = b = 1 to start with and carrying out this mapping repeatedly on each new (reduced) rational number gives the following sequence 1/1, 3/2, 7/5, 17/12, 41/29, ... converging to 2^(1/2). Sequence contains the numerators. - [Amarnath Murthy](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Amarnath_Murthy), Mar 22 2003 [Amended by Paul E. Black (paul.black(AT)nist.gov), Dec 18 2006] Odd-indexed prime numerators are prime RMS numbers ([A140480](https://oeis.org/A140480)) and also NSW primes ([A088165](https://oeis.org/A088165)). - [Ctibor O. Zizka](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Ctibor_O._Zizka), Aug 13 2008 The intermediate convergents to 2^(1/2) begin with 4/3, 10/7, 24/17, 58/41; essentially, numerators=[A052542](https://oeis.org/A052542) and denominators here. - [Clark Kimberling](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Clark_Kimberling), Aug 26 2008 Equals right border of triangle [A143966](https://oeis.org/A143966). Starting (1, 3, 7, ...) equals INVERT transform of (1, 2, 2, 2, ...) and row sums of triangle [A143966](https://oeis.org/A143966). - [Gary W. Adamson](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Gary_W._Adamson), Sep 06 2008 Inverse binomial transform of [A006012](https://oeis.org/A006012); Hankel transform is := [1, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, ...]. - [Philippe Deléham](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Philippe_Del%C3%A9ham), Dec 04 2008 From [Charlie Marion](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Charlie_Marion), Jan 07 2009: (Start) In general, denominators, a(k,n) and numerators, b(k,n), of continued fraction convergents to sqrt((k+1)/k) may be found as follows: let a(k,0) = 1, a(k,1) = 2k; for n>0, a(k,2n) = 2*a(k,2n-1) + a(k,2n-2) and a(k,2n+1) = (2k)*a(k,2n) + a(k,2n-1); let b(k,0) = 1, b(k,1) = 2k+1; for n>0, b(k,2n) = 2*b(k,2n-1) + b(k,2n-2) and b(k,2n+1) = (2k)*b(k,2n) + b(k,2n-1). For example, the convergents to sqrt(2/1) start 1/1, 3/2, 7/5, 17/12, 41/29. In general, if a(k,n) and b(k,n) are the denominators and numerators, respectively, of continued fraction convergents to sqrt((k+1)/k) as defined above, then k*a(k,2n)^2 - a(k,2n-1)*a(k,2n+1) = k = k*a(k,2n-2)*a(k,2n) - a(k,2n-1)^2 and b(k,2n-1)*b(k,2n+1) - k*b(k,2n)^2 = k+1 = b(k,2n-1)^2 - k*b(k,2n-2)*b(k,2n); for example, if k=1 and n=3, then b(1,n)=a(n+1) and 1*a(1,6)^2 - a(1,5)*a(1,7) = 1*169^2 - 70*408 = 1; 1*a(1,4)*a(1,6) - a(1,5)^2 = 1*29*169 - 70^2 = 1; b(1,5)*b(1,7) - 1*b(1,6)^2 = 99*577 - 1*239^2 = 2; b(1,5)^2 - 1*b(1,4)*b(1,6) = 99^2 - 1*41*239 = 2. Cf. [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129), [A142238](https://oeis.org/A142238)-[A142239](https://oeis.org/A142239), [A153313](https://oeis.org/A153313)-[A153318](https://oeis.org/A153318). (End) This sequence occurs in the lower bound of the order of the set of equivalent resistances of n equal resistors combined in series and in parallel ([A048211](https://oeis.org/A048211)). - [Sameen Ahmed Khan](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Sameen_Ahmed_Khan), Jun 28 2010 Let M = a triangle with the Fibonacci series in each column, but the leftmost column is shifted upwards one row. [A001333](https://oeis.org/A001333) = lim_{n->infinity} M^n, the left-shifted vector considered as a sequence. - [Gary W. Adamson](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Gary_W._Adamson), Jul 27 2010 a(n) is the number of compositions of n when there are 1 type of 1 and 2 types of other natural numbers. - [Milan Janjic](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Milan_Janjic), Aug 13 2010 Equals the INVERTi transform of [A055099](https://oeis.org/A055099). - [Gary W. Adamson](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Gary_W._Adamson), Aug 14 2010 From [L. Edson Jeffery](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:L._Edson_Jeffery), Apr 04 2011: (Start) Let U be the unit-primitive matrix (see [Jeffery]) U = U_(8,2) = (0 0 1 0)  (0 1 0 1)  (1 0 2 0)  (0 2 0 1). Then a(n) = (1/4)*Trace(U^n). (See also [A084130](https://oeis.org/A084130), [A006012](https://oeis.org/A006012).) (End) For n >= 1, row sums of triangle  m/k.|..0.....1.....2.....3.....4.....5.....6.....7  ==================================================  .0..|..1  .1..|..1.....2  .2..|..1.....2.....4  .3..|..1.....4.....4.....8  .4..|..1.....4....12.....8....16  .5..|..1.....6....12....32....16....32  .6..|..1.....6....24....32....80....32....64  .7..|..1.....8....24....80....80...192....64...128 which is the triangle for numbers 2^k*C(m,k) with duplicated diagonals. - [Vladimir Shevelev](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Vladimir_Shevelev), Apr 12 2012 a(n) is also the number of ways to place k non-attacking wazirs on a 2 X n board, summed over all k >= 0 (a wazir is a leaper [0,1]). - [Vaclav Kotesovec](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Vaclav_Kotesovec), May 08 2012 The sequences a(n) and b(n) := [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n) are entries of powers of the special case of the Brahmagupta Matrix - for details see Suryanarayan's paper. Further, as Suryanarayan remark, if we set A = 2*(a(n) + b(n))*b(n), B = a(n)*(a(n) + 2*b(n)), C = a(n)^2 + 2*a(n)*b(n) + 2*b(n)^2 we obtain integral solutions of the Pythagorean relation A^2 + B^2 = C^2, where A and B are consecutive integers. - [Roman Witula](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Roman_Witula), Jul 28 2012 Pisano period lengths: 1, 1, 8, 4, 12, 8, 6, 4, 24, 12, 24, 8, 28, 6, 24, 8, 16, 24, 40, 12, .... - [R. J. Mathar](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:R._J._Mathar), Aug 10 2012 This sequence and [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129) give the diagonal numbers described by Theon of Smyrna. - [Sture Sjöstedt](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Sture_Sj%C3%B6stedt), Oct 20 2012 a(n) is the top left entry of the n-th power of any of the following six 3 X 3 binary matrices: [1, 1, 1; 1, 1, 1; 1, 0, 0] or [1, 1, 1; 1, 1, 0; 1, 1, 0] or [1, 1, 1; 1, 0, 1; 1, 1, 0] or [1, 1, 1; 1, 1, 0; 1, 0, 1] or [1, 1, 1; 1, 0, 1; 1, 0, 1] or [1, 1, 1; 1, 0, 0; 1, 1, 1]. - [R. J. Mathar](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:R._J._Mathar), Feb 03 2014 If p is prime, a(p) == 1 (mod p) (compare with similar comment for [A000032](https://oeis.org/A000032)). - [Creighton Dement](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Creighton_Dement), Oct 11 2005, modified by [Davide Colazingari](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Davide_Colazingari), Jun 26 2016 a(n) = [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n) + [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n-1), where [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n) is the n-th Pell Number; e.g., a(6) = 99 = [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(6) + [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(5) = 70 + 29. Hence the sequence of fractions has the form 1 + [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n-1)/[A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n), and the ratio [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n-1)/[A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n)converges to sqrt(2) - 1. - [Gregory L. Simay](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Gregory_L._Simay), Nov 30 2018 For n > 0, a(n+1) is the length of tau^n(1) where tau is the morphism: 1 -> 101, 0 -> 1. See Song and Wu. - [Michel Marcus](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Michel_Marcus), Jul 21 2020 For n > 0, a(n) is the number of nonisomorphic quasitrivial semigroups with n elements, see Devillet, Marichal, Teheux. [A292932](https://oeis.org/A292932) is the number of labeled quasitrivial semigroups. - [Peter Jipsen](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Peter_Jipsen), Mar 28 2021 a(n) is the permanent of the n X n tridiagonal matrix defined in [A332602](https://oeis.org/A332602). - [Stefano Spezia](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Stefano_Spezia), Apr 12 2022 From [Greg Dresden](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Greg_Dresden), May 08 2023: (Start) For n >= 2, 4*a(n) is the number of ways to tile this T-shaped figure of length n-1 with two colors of squares and one color of domino; shown here is the figure of length 5 (corresponding to n=6), and it has 4*a(6) = 396 different tilings.  _  |_|_ _ _ _  |_|_|_|_|_|  |_| (End) 12*a(n) = number of walks of length n in the cyclic Kautz digraph CK(3,4). - [Miquel A. FORMULA  a(n) = [A055642](https://oeis.org/A055642)([A125058](https://oeis.org/A125058)(n)). - [Reinhard Zumkeller](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Reinhard_Zumkeller), Feb 02 2007 a(n) = 2a(n-1) + a(n-2); a(n) = ((1-sqrt(2))^n + (1+sqrt(2))^n)/2. a(n)+a(n+1) = 2 [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n+1). 2*a(n) = [A002203](https://oeis.org/A002203)(n). G.f.: (1 - x) / (1 - 2*x - x^2) = 1 / (1 - x / (1 - 2*x / (1 + x))). - [Simon Plouffe](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Simon_Plouffe) in his 1992 dissertation. [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(2n) = 2*[A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n)*a(n). - [John McNamara](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:John_McNamara), Oct 30 2002 a(n) = (-i)^n * T(n, i), with T(n, x) Chebyshev's polynomials of the first kind [A053120](https://oeis.org/A053120) and i^2 = -1. a(n) = a(n-1) + [A052542](https://oeis.org/A052542)(n-1), n>1. a(n)/[A052542](https://oeis.org/A052542)(n) converges to sqrt(1/2). - Mario Catalani (mario.catalani(AT)unito.it), Apr 29 2003 E.g.f.: exp(x)cosh(x*sqrt(2)). - [Paul Barry](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Paul_Barry), May 08 2003 a(n) = Sum_{k=0..floor(n/2)} binomial(n, 2k)2^k. - [Paul Barry](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Paul_Barry), May 13 2003 For n > 0, a(n)^2 - (1 + (-1)^(n))/2 = Sum_{k=0..n-1} ((2k+1)*[A001653](https://oeis.org/A001653)(n-1-k)); e.g., 17^2 - 1 = 288 = 1*169 + 3*29 + 5*5 + 7*1; 7^2 = 49 = 1*29 + 3*5 + 5*1. - [Charlie Marion](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Charlie_Marion), Jul 18 2003 a(n+2) = [A078343](https://oeis.org/A078343)(n+1) + [A048654](https://oeis.org/A048654)(n). - [Creighton Dement](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Creighton_Dement), Jan 19 2005 a(n) = [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n) + [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n-1) = [A001109](https://oeis.org/A001109)(n)/[A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n) = sqrt([A001110](https://oeis.org/A001110)(n)/[A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n)^2) = ceiling(sqrt([A001108](https://oeis.org/A001108)(n))). - [Henry Bottomley](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Henry_Bottomley), Apr 18 2000 Also the first differences of [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129) (the Pell numbers) because [A052937](https://oeis.org/A052937)(n) = [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n+1) + 1. - [Graeme McRae](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Graeme_McRae), Aug 03 2006 a(n) = Sum_{k=0..n} [A122542](https://oeis.org/A122542)(n,k). - [Philippe Deléham](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Philippe_Del%C3%A9ham), Oct 08 2006 For another recurrence see [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129). a(n) = Sum_{k=0..n} [A098158](https://oeis.org/A098158)(n,k)*2^(n-k). - [Philippe Deléham](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Philippe_Del%C3%A9ham), Dec 26 2007 a(n) = upper left and lower right terms of [1,1; 2,1]^n. - [Gary W. Adamson](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Gary_W._Adamson), Mar 12 2008 If p[1]=1, and p[i]=2, (i>1), and if A is Hessenberg matrix of order n defined by: A[i,j]=p[j-i+1], (i<=j), A[i,j]=-1, (i=j+1), and A[i,j]=0 otherwise. Then, for n>=1, a(n)=det A. - [Milan Janjic](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Milan_Janjic), Apr 29 2010 For n>=2, a(n)=F_n(2)+F_(n+1)(2), where F_n(x) is Fibonacci polynomial (cf. Mathar](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:R._J._Mathar), Feb 05 2024 From [Peter Bala](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Peter_Bala), Jul 06 2025: (Start) G.f.: Sum_{n >= 1} (-1)^(n+1) * x^(n-1) * Product_{k = 1..n} (1 - k*x)/(1 - 3*x + k*x^2). The following series telescope: Sum_{n >= 1} (-1)^(n+1)/(a(2*n) + 1/a(2*n)) = 1/4, since 1/(a(2*n) + 1/a(2*n)) = 1/[A077445](https://oeis.org/A077445)(n) + 1/[A077445](https://oeis.org/A077445)(n+1). Sum_{n >= 1} (-1)^(n+1)/(a(2*n+1) - 1/a(2*n+1)) = 1/8, since. 1/(a(2*n+1) - 1/a(2*n+1)) = 1/(4*Pell(2*n)) + 1/(4*Pell(2*n+2)), where Pell(n) = [A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129)(n). Sum_{n >= 1} (-1)^(n+1)/(a(2*n+1) + 9/a(2*n+1)) = 1/10, since 1/(a(2*n+1) + 9/a(2*n+1)) = b(n) + b(n+1), where b(n) = [A001109](https://oeis.org/A001109)(n)/(2*Pell(2*n-1)*Pell(2*n+1)). Sum_{n >= 1} (-1)^(n+1)/(a(n)*a(n+1)) = 1 - sqrt(2)/2 = [A268682](https://oeis.org/A268682), since (-1)^(n+1)/(a(n)*a(n+1)) = Pell(n)/a(n) - Pell(n+1)/a(n+1). (End) a(n) = hypergeom([-n/2,(1-n)/2], [1/2], 2). - [Victor Petrescu](https://oeis.org/wiki/User:Victor_Petrescu), Nov 06 2025    EXAMPLE  Convergents are 1, 3/2, 7/5, 17/12, 41/29, 99/70, 239/169, 577/408, 1393/985, 3363/2378, 8119/5741, 19601/13860, 47321/33461, 114243/80782, ... = [A001333](https://oeis.org/A001333)/[A000129](https://oeis.org/A000129).
